returns.name: Michigan annual withholding return
contents: All businesses file an annual return by February 28, regardless of assigned filing frequency.
Income record forms (W-2, 1099) are filed under Michigan's Income Record Form Remittance Guide.

returns.name: Michigan monthly or quarterly withholding return
contents: Monthly filers: by the 20th of the following month; quarterly filers: by the 20th of the month after the quarter.
EFT payments are due the 20th of the following month.

notModelled: Michigan's ACCELERATED schedule (same day as the federal payment; pre-payment by the 20th and a reconciliation by the 20th of the next month): the rule is stated but follows the federal schedule and is not modelled.
The thresholds Treasury uses to assign monthly, quarterly or annual: not on the page.
Michigan unemployment insurance (Unemployment Insurance Agency): no document read.
Michigan's State-holiday list (weekends only are skipped, with a warning).
City income tax withholding (Michigan cities file separately).
The Income Record Form Remittance Guide's file layouts.

deposits.interpretation: Treasury determines each year whether an employer files MONTHLY, QUARTERLY or ANNUALLY; the page gives no thresholds, so the frequency is an INPUT and is never derived. Monthly: return and payment by the 20th of the following month. Quarterly: by the 20th of the month after the quarter (April 20, July 20, October 20, January 20). Every business also files an ANNUAL return by February 28 regardless of its frequency; an annual filer pays by then. ACCELERATED filers (EFT only) must remit on or before the same day as their federal payments regardless of the amount: a pre-payment by the 20th of the current month and a reconciliation payment by the 20th of the next month for the remaining liability. The accelerated schedule follows the federal deposit schedule and is NOT MODELLED: supplying 'accelerated' returns an error rather than a guess. A due date on a weekend or State holiday moves to the next business day.
